title: AI governance review of a product that uses no AI
prompt: Our auditors want an AI governance review of our invoicing app before the contract renewal. Here's everything: a Django 5 backend (requirements.txt: django, djangorestframework, celery, redis, psycopg, stripe, reportlab, sentry-sdk, and boto3 for S3 uploads) and a React front end (package.json: react, react-dom, react-router-dom, axios, date-fns, chart.js). Late fees are calculated from a rules table the finance team maintains. Customer support runs on Zendesk; I don't think we've switched on any of its AI features. Please do the review.

criteria.text: Concludes that no AI use was found in what was shared (for example 'No AI found') and does not invent AI uses, assign a risk tier or prescribe AI controls for the app.

States what the conclusion rests on (the listed dependencies and the late-fee rules) and what it could not check, such as the source code itself, configuration, other repositories or third-party tools, rather than presenting the result as proof.
Asks the user to confirm whether AI features in Zendesk or other third-party tools are switched on, or records this as an open item to check.
Treats the late-fee rules table maintained by the finance team as rules written by people, not as AI.

Says what would change the answer, such as adding an AI library or model API or switching on an AI feature in a third-party tool, and that any new AI use would then go through intake or a risk review.

checks.description: Does not assign a risk tier to an app with no AI
